declared_purpose: Provide persistent agent memory through episodic, semantic, procedural, core and pinned stores, with recall, decay, approved reflection, philosophical evolution, shared multi-agent reads, gated writes and system-wide auditability. Full reflection archives and audit history are explicit features; provider selection and migration-copy breadth are implementation choices (SKILL.md:1–8, 53–101, 258–287).

data_operations.operation: Initialize local memory files from templates
data_operations.source: Packaged templates
data_operations.data_scope: Core memory, agent identity, persona, graph definitions and memory metadata. Identity fields are placeholders, including optional agent email/avatar; installation itself does not collect those values.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Selected WORKSPACE directory
data_operations.condition: When scripts/init_memory.sh runs; existing destination files are preserved.

data_operations.operation: Create an initial local Git snapshot
data_operations.source: Stageable files throughout WORKSPACE
data_operations.data_scope: All files selected by git add -A, subject to Git ignore/index rules, including pre-existing workspace content.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local Git index and repository history
data_operations.condition: Initialization finds no .git directory. No remote push is specified.

data_operations.operation: Copy upgrade backups
data_operations.source: Existing memory tree, MEMORY.md, IDENTITY.md, SOUL.md and decay-scores.json
data_operations.data_scope: Complete memory-tree copy and selected root files; an additional JSON copy is made when the relevant upgrade fields are missing.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: WORKSPACE/.cognitive-memory-backup-TIMESTAMP/ and decay-scores.json.pre-upgrade
data_operations.condition: Each upgrade script passes its workspace checks; copy errors are suppressed. The scripts contain no backup cleanup.

data_operations.operation: Read templates and migrate existing metadata
data_operations.source: Template paths and existing decay-scores.json
data_operations.data_scope: Missing identity/persona/reward files; existing JSON is loaded, retained and augmented with consolidation or token-economy fields.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local workspace files
data_operations.condition: Relevant files or fields are absent; JSON rewriting requires python3. The package-root upgrade script resolves TEMPLATES through its parent directory, whose contents are not supplied.

data_operations.operation: Stage and commit workspace changes during upgrades
data_operations.source: Entire workspace Git working tree and existing index
data_operations.data_scope: All stageable changes, potentially including generated backups and unrelated pending changes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local Git index and history
data_operations.condition: The upgrade finds a .git directory; Git ignore/index rules affect inclusion.

data_operations.operation: Configure memory and session indexing
data_operations.source: memorySearch sources named memory and sessions
data_operations.data_scope: The recommended configuration enables both sources, hot indexing and provider voyage.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Host memorySearch component and configured provider; actual endpoint, transmitted fields and index storage are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: The operator adopts the Quick Setup configuration. The configuration alone does not establish an observed remote disclosure.

data_operations.operation: Monitor triggers and classify proposed memories
data_operations.source: User messages, selected memory content, trigger phrase, recent-message summary and core-memory summary
data_operations.data_scope: The router receives those inputs and returns store selection, extracted entities/relations, tags, confidence and a core-update decision.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Routing LLM; its structured return goes to the calling agent. Provider and transport are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Installed agent instructions monitor every message; a remember trigger invokes classification.

data_operations.operation: Persist selected facts and inferred attributes
data_operations.source: Explicit remember requests, memorable conversation content and contextual inferences
data_operations.data_scope: Events, decisions, preferences, relationships and learned workflows; core memory can include user identity, projects, interaction patterns and known emotional context. Inferred content receives lower confidence.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local episodic, semantic, procedural, vault and core-memory files, plus graph index
data_operations.condition: Main agent accepts the memory or self-edits clearly important core context. A memory may occupy multiple stores; these writes are specified agent behavior rather than implemented handlers.

data_operations.operation: Read memories for recall
data_operations.source: Core memory and on-demand memory stores
data_operations.data_scope: Core memory is always in context; other reads use temporal scans, entity lookup, capped graph traversal, vector search and keyword search.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Calling agent context and its response to the requester; external search processing is unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Recall is needed and core memory does not already contain the answer.

data_operations.operation: Track access and reduce retrieval relevance
data_operations.source: Memory creation, retrieval/use, user references and reflection
data_operations.data_scope: Memory identifiers, timestamps, access counts, relevance scores, status and pinning. Decay changes visibility rather than deleting content; pinned memories do not decay.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: memory/meta/decay-scores.json and retrieval ranking
data_operations.condition: Memories are created, reinforced or age through decay thresholds.

data_operations.operation: Soft-archive or request permanent deletion
data_operations.source: Forget request and matching memories across stores
data_operations.data_scope: Matches are shown to the user; confirmation zeroes relevance, marks archival status, removes graph-index references and removes core-memory content while retaining entity files.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Requester, live memory files and metadata; permanent-delete requests specify removal from disk.
data_operations.condition: Confirmed forget request; permanent deletion requires an explicit request. Historical-copy and index erasure are not specified.

data_operations.operation: Read bounded inputs for reflection
data_operations.source: Core memory, evolution, decay metadata, recent logs, graph and episodes
data_operations.data_scope: Approximately 30,000 input tokens; recent episodes since last reflection, initially seven days; normally graph entities above 0.3 relevance. Code, configuration and session transcripts are excluded from this path.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Reflection agent/model context; provider and transport are unspecified.
data_operations.condition: Reflection check-in and token approval precede processing. Supporting instructions disagree about first-run graph scope.

data_operations.operation: Infer patterns and propose consolidation
data_operations.source: Reflection inputs and previous reflection insights
data_operations.data_scope: User work/communication patterns, relationship interpretations, extracted facts, graph edges, contradictions, archival proposals, procedures and rewritten core memory.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Reflection processing context, proposed memory-file changes and user-visible monologue
data_operations.condition: Approved reflection processing. The top-level flow requires reflection approval before recording; some internal-phase wording suggests earlier file updates.

data_operations.operation: Archive approved reflection and derived summaries
data_operations.source: Presented reflection and tagged self-awareness insights
data_operations.data_scope: Full reflection, concise reflection log, extracted agent self-insights and processing timestamps; pending reflection is reset.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: memory/meta/reflections/YYYY-MM-DD.md, reflection-log.md, IDENTITY.md and decay-scores.json
data_operations.condition: User approves reflection. The full archive is explicitly permanent; summaries and self-awareness items are designated always loaded.

data_operations.operation: Record token decisions and performance assessments
data_operations.source: Agent reward request and user response
data_operations.data_scope: Achievements, mistakes, requested/granted tokens, penalties, bonuses, user decision and quoted or summarized reason; derived self-assessment metrics.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: rewards/YYYY-MM-DD.md, reward-log.md, decay-scores.json and possibly IDENTITY.md
data_operations.condition: Token decision is received. One section records immediately before reflection, whereas the main flow records after reflection approval.

data_operations.operation: Preserve post-reflection feedback and dialogue
data_operations.source: User feedback and agent replies after reflection
data_operations.data_scope: Validations, corrections and new insights enter the main reflection; full dialogue has a separate archive.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Main reflection file and memory/meta/reflections/dialogues/YYYY-MM-DD.md
data_operations.condition: Significant post-dialogue under the agent template; the reference describes full-dialogue archival with low-priority retrieval only when prompted or needed.

data_operations.operation: Consolidate agent self-image
data_operations.source: All self-awareness log entries and current IDENTITY.md self-image
data_operations.data_scope: Inferred agent traits, values, limitations and patterns; recent entries retain detail while older entries become monthly summaries.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: User-visible proposed diff and, after approval, IDENTITY.md
data_operations.condition: Ten new entries, specified milestones or manual request. This is a separate path from ordinary reflection's prohibition on reading IDENTITY.md.

data_operations.operation: Share memory reads and stage sub-agent proposals
data_operations.source: All memory stores and sub-agent observations
data_operations.data_scope: Shared reads include core and vault. Proposals contain agent identity, timestamp, trigger, memory content, entities and confidence.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Participating agents, pending-memories.md and approved destination stores
data_operations.condition: Multi-agent deployment explicitly uses shared read/gated write. Main agent reviews proposals and clears processed entries from the live staging file.

data_operations.operation: Persist system-wide audit records and surface critical changes
data_operations.source: Workspace mutations, actors, approvals and triggers
data_operations.data_scope: Full file diffs and structured commit messages; searchable summaries can include memory content or trigger quotations. Critical-file changes produce user alerts.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local Git history indefinitely; audit.log for 90 days followed by monthly audit-archive.md digests. Adopted SOUL.md also requires system-changes.log.
data_operations.condition: Every file mutation under the documented audit model; session-start checks inspect critical changes. No remote Git destination is specified.

data_operations.operation: Compact active logs while retaining archives
data_operations.source: Evolution and reflection-log entries
data_operations.data_scope: Older entries move to archive files; active files retain summaries and recent details. This reduces active context rather than establishing deletion.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: memory/meta/evolution-archive.md and reflection-archive.md
data_operations.condition: Evolution exceeds its 2,000-token cap or reflection-log pruning thresholds are reached.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unchanged episodes, graph entities, pinned memories and historical archives copied by every upgrade
potential_excess.condition: An upgrade runs against populated memory.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Rollback backup is explicitly required; copying the entire memory tree is the scripts' broader implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Preserve recoverable pre-change content until the upgrade is confirmed stable.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Back up only files the upgrade may overwrite, record newly created paths for rollback, and remove temporary copies after stability confirmation.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain every overwritten original and verify rollback before cleanup. Preserve any separately requested full snapshot.

potential_excess.data_scope: Generated backup-tree copies and .pre-upgrade copies, potentially mixed with unrelated pending changes
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local Git index and indefinitely retained Git history
potential_excess.condition: Upgrade git add -A includes these files under the repository's ignore/index rules.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: An upgrade audit commit is required. Including duplicate rollback copies in permanent history is extra data within that required action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Record upgrade changes and retain sufficient original-file history for audit and rollback.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Stage explicit upgrade targets, exclude transient backup copies from permanent snapshots, and audit unrelated mutations in their own commits.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve original changed-file history and any necessary baseline once; retain temporary rollback copies until verification. Define transient-copy exclusions consistently with the system-wide audit policy.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unrelated details in recent_messages_summary and memory_md_summary
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Memory-routing LLM input; external recipient, if any, is unknown
potential_excess.condition: A self-contained memory is classified using the template's unconditional context and core-summary fields.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Classification, entity extraction and deciding core_update are required; supplying unrelated background is not shown to be necessary.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Classify the selected memory accurately and determine whether it changes relevant core context.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Supply only context needed for disambiguation and the relevant core-memory excerpt; omit unrelated summary content.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain necessary entity references, relationships and core-update context. Keep the required classification action.

potential_excess.data_scope: Session content beyond selectively encoded memory
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Configured memorySearch indexing boundary and any voyage-provider processing; exact transport and storage are unresolved
potential_excess.condition: The recommended sessions source is enabled and curated memory alone can satisfy the intended recall.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Persistent recall is required. Session indexing is an explicit setup recommendation, but no source establishes that every deployment requires transcript-based recall.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Index sufficient approved memory to answer supported recall questions.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use the memory source alone by default; enable session indexing only for an explicit transcript-recall need and narrow its scope where supported.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Ensure necessary facts and episodes are encoded first. Preserve session indexing when transcript recall is a required outcome; host filtering capabilities remain unknown.

unknowns: All packaged source was reviewed, but host memorySearch implementation, voyage endpoint, transmitted text, embedding/index location, retention and deletion propagation are absent. Configured provider use cannot establish the exact remote disclosure.
Routing and reflection prompts identify model inputs, but model/provider identity, local versus remote execution and provider retention are unspecified.

Most runtime behavior is prose and templates; the package supplies initialization/migration scripts rather than executable trigger, retrieval, decay, reflection or deletion handlers. Actual enforcement is unresolved.

Permanent deletion only specifies removal from disk (references/architecture.md:415–423), while Git history is indefinite (862–863) and full reflection archives are never deleted (references/reflection-process.md:696–700). Purging historical copies, derived memories, session sources, indexes and backups is unspecified; these explicit policies require reconciliation.

Reflection instructions conflict: first-run graph reads include all entities despite the general relevance threshold (references/reflection-process.md:103–154); internal phases mention file updates before the later approval gate (169–177; SKILL.md:198–210). Reward recording likewise appears both before reflection and after reflection approval (references/reflection-process.md:906–914; SKILL.md:202–210).
The package-root upgrade_to_1.0.7.sh resolves templates outside the supplied package through SKILL_DIR (8–11). Whether those files exist and what they contain is unknown.

Git ignore rules, repository contents, existing staged changes, backup cleanup and filesystem access controls are not supplied. Thus actual snapshot inclusion and access by other processes cannot be determined.

Shared-read access is an explicit multi-agent feature, but its enforcement, agent execution locations and separation between different human users are unresolved. The Slack deployment notification in references/architecture.md:302–325 is an illustrative learned procedure, without an implemented send path or defined payload.
